FPGA Implementation of a PatchCore-lite
Anomaly Detection System
with Category-wise Profile Switching
Shunya Yamada and Kazuyoshi Takagi

Computer Architecture Laboratory, Department of Information Engineering,
Graduate School of Engineering, Mie University  |  shunya@arch.info.mie-u.ac.jp
1  PatchCore anomaly detection

PatchCore [1] detects defects by comparing image features with stored
normal examples. A memory bank is a set of representative normal patch
features.
bullets: PatchCore [1] detects defects by comparing image features with stored normal examples.

items.text: 2  Category-wise profile and bank switching

Useful feature settings differ between categories. A known product
category selects its profile and normal memory bank before inspection.
The proposed FPGA design shares one CNN and NN engine.
bullets: Before inspection, the known category selects its feature profile and normal memory bank.
The proposed FPGA design shares one CNN and NN engine.

items.text: 3  Experiment and comparison

Dataset: MVTec AD [2], all 15 categories.
Tasks: all 105 pairs and all 455 triples.
Backbone: shared WideResNet50-2.
Bank: k-center coreset, 3,000 vectors/category.

Profile selection: a prior single-category sweep at bank=12,000 retained
candidates within 2 percentage points of the default normal-pass rate, then
minimized patch count × feature dimension.

items.text:
One shared CNN and NN engine use profile registers and bank address
control. Switching requires register updates rather than a new bitstream. Fewer
bank reads and distance calculations may reduce latency and energy.
bullets: One shared CNN and NN engine use profile registers and bank address control.
Switching requires register updates rather than a new bitstream.
Fewer bank reads and distance calculations may reduce latency and energy.

items.text:
Implement the mode-controlled NN pipeline in RTL/HLS. Check 8-bit accuracy,
switching overhead and memory stalls. Synthesis and board tests will quantify
LUT/DSP/BRAM use, end-to-end latency and power.
